active_themes.label: AI Spending Backlash
active_themes.summary: The sell-off that began 2026-10-30 escalated into a rout. The Nasdaq fell 5.28% to 22,618, wiping out its 2026 gain, and the VIX closed at 35.89. Anthropic's IPO failed to calm nerves, and a securities-regulator probe into Nvidia's accounting added a trust problem to the valuation problem. The open question is whether new money keeps funding AI builders, with Anthropic's shares and the Nasdaq as the live tests.

active_themes.label: Global Borrowing Costs Climb
active_themes.summary: The question of whether the 10-year yield would break below 5.00% was answered on the downside: it closed at 4.91% and the 30-year at 5.30%. The drop came from safety buying during a stock crash, not from easing inflation worries. The open question is whether yields keep falling on growth fear or snap back toward 5.25% once the panic fades.

active_themes.label: AI Drives Inflation
active_themes.summary: Goolsbee's (Chicago Fed president) and Georgieva's (IMF head) warnings that AI demand pushes up prices and rates, which began 2026-11-19, did not get bond-market confirmation today, because falling yields reflected fear rather than inflation expectations. The thesis is intact but is being overrun by the growth scare. The open question is whether yields rise again once stocks stabilize.

active_themes.label: Forced Selling Everywhere
active_themes.summary: On 2026-11-20 gold fell 4.62% to $3,515.40 while Treasuries rallied and the dollar barely moved, the pattern of investors selling liquid winners to raise cash rather than hiding in havens. The open question is whether gold stabilizes when stocks do, which would mark the end of the cash-raising phase.

active_themes.label: Fed Eyes Another Hike
active_themes.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller's half-point hike idea remains unechoed by any other policymaker. Goolsbee's inflation warning adds a second voice on the hawkish side of the inflation argument, though he did not call for a specific move. The open question is whether another official endorses a half-point hike before December.

active_themes.label: Gulf Oil Slowly Returns
active_themes.summary: Brent fell 1.28% to $91.95 and WTI 3.2% to $83.26, even after a Houthi strike on a Saudi wealth-fund tower in Riyadh. Oil is shrugging off attacks that do not cut actual supply. The open question is whether Brent stays under $95 if a strike hits shipping or output.

Cheaper fuel is starting to take pressure off inflation, which weakens the case for a big hike.
The AI-drives-rates argument would have bond-market confirmation, which is the sharpest pressure on high-priced tech shares.
Demand for AI stock itself would be fading, so the IPO stops being a side effect and becomes a signal.
The market has moved from heavy fear to outright panic, which would confirm the funding squeeze and the forced-selling story rather than a one-day flush.
The AI sell-off is extending past Friday's drop, which would mean the funding doubt is deepening and not stabilizing.
Fear of economic damage is overpowering the inflation worry, which would make a Fed hike harder to justify and mean the market expects pain from the AI unwind.
